(sec-module-symbolics.advancedsolvers)=
# Module: symbolics.advancedSolvers

Implicit solvers beyond those of Exudyn's C++ core, for the systems of exudyn.symbolics.systemModel:
SolveTrapezoidalGGL integrates a SymbolicSystemBase by the trapezoidal rule with the position and the
velocity constraints enforced by the stabilization of Gear, Gupta and Leimkuhler (GGL), with constant steps
or with a step size controlled by the local error estimated from the accelerations (#3242). They take the
SimulationSettings of Exudyn and write their output as the solvers of exudyn.symbolics.solvers.

- **Author**: Johannes Gerstmayr
- **Date**: 2026-11-04 (created)

(sec-advancedsolvers-solvetrapezoidalggl)=
## Function: SolveTrapezoidalGGL

[`SolveTrapezoidalGGL(system, simulationSettings = None)`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/symbolics/advancedSolvers.py#L136)

- **function description**: the implicit time integration of a SymbolicSystemBase by the trapezoidal rule with the stabilization of Gear, Gupta and Leimkuhler (GGL) for index-3 constraints (#3242): per step v1 = v0 + h/2 (a0 + a1), q1 = q0 + h/2 (v0 + v1) - C_q^T mu, M a1 = f(q1, v1, t1) - C_q^T z1, c(q1, t1) = 0 and C_q v1 + c_t = 0, with C_q = C_q(q1) - in the term of mu that of the previous Newton iterate -, the multiplier mu of the velocity constraints, which moves the positions back onto the constraints, and the ODE1 coordinates by the trapezoidal rule as well; Newton's method for a1, y1, z1 and mu with the Jacobian of the system, the ODE2 rows scaled by h^2/4 and the algebraic columns by its inverse, as Exudyn's implicit solver; of the second derivatives of the constraints only (C_q v)_q in the Jacobian. The method is of order 2 in q, v, the accelerations and z, and does not damp; the constraints hold on position and velocity level in every step. The algebraic equations must depend on q and t only; C_q comes from the reaction forces of the system. With timeIntegration.automaticStepSize (the default, as for the explicit solvers DOPRI5 and ODE23) the step size is controlled by the local errors of the positions, h^3/12 q_ttt = h^2/12 (a1 - a0), and of the velocities, h^3/12 a_tt by the second difference of the mean accelerations (v1 - v0)/h of the last three steps - the accelerations a of the trapezoidal rule alternate with constraints, their means do not -, with the PI controller of _ErrorStepSize and timeIntegration.absoluteTolerance, relativeTolerance, stepSizeSafety, stepSizeMaxIncrease, initialStepSize and minimumStepSize, the maximum step (endTime - startTime)/numberOfSteps; the tolerances are those of a step, the global error grows with the number of steps and with the sensitivity of the motion. The ODE1 coordinates are not in the estimate. Without automaticStepSize the steps are constant, as SolveGeneralizedAlpha. The initial accelerations and algebraic coordinates are consistent ([M C_q^T; C_q 0] [a0; z0] = [f; -(C_q v)_q v]), the initial ODE1 velocities those of the ODE1 equations. Newton's method by timeIntegration.newton (relativeTolerance, absoluteTolerance, maxIterations, useModifiedNewton, weightTolerancePerCoordinate); a step whose Newton iteration does not converge or diverges is repeated with a smaller step with automaticStepSize or adaptiveStep, else raises. Data coordinates and adaptiveStep as SolveGeneralizedAlpha; the output - the result, and for a SymbolicSystem the solution file, the sensors and the renderer of its mbs - as the solvers of exudyn.symbolics.solvers, at the exact write times
- **input**:
  - `system`: the system, a SymbolicSystemBase
  - `simulationSettings`: exudyn.SimulationSettings; None: the defaults
- **output**: dict with 'time' (n_out), 'q', 'q_t', 'q_tt' (n_out x nODE2), with ODE1 coordinates 'y', 'y_t', with algebraic equations 'z', at the times of solution.file.writePeriod and the end, and the statistics 'steps', 'newtonIterations', 'jacobianEvaluations', 'discontinuousIterations', 'rejectedSteps' (by Newton or the post-Newton step) and 'rejectedStepsError' (by the error estimate)


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`symbolicLobatto4Test.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/symbolicLobatto4Test.py) (TM), [`symbolicTrapezoidalGGLStepSizeTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/symbolicTrapezoidalGGLStepSizeTest.py) (TM), [`symbolicTrapezoidalGGLTest.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/symbolicTrapezoidalGGLTest.py) (TM)


(sec-advancedsolvers-solveimplicitrungekutta)=
## Function: SolveImplicitRungeKutta

[`SolveImplicitRungeKutta(system, simulationSettings = None, method = 'LobattoIIIA4')`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/exudyn/symbolics/advancedSolvers.py#L528)

- **function description**: the implicit time integration of a SymbolicSystemBase by an implicit Runge-Kutta method for index-3 constraints (#3244, #3246, #3247), of implicitRungeKuttaMethods, each with two implicit stages: - 'LobattoIIIA4': Lobatto IIIA with the stages at the start, the middle and the end of the step, the constraints and the velocity constraints at the end of the step only and a multiplier per stage after the start, the one of the start that of the end of the previous step; of order 4 in q and v, without numerical damping, it keeps the energy - the simplest form that solves index 3 directly; - 'LobattoIIIC4-GGL': Lobatto IIIC, the stages at the same times, the first implicit as well, with the constraints and the velocity constraints at each stage and its positions moved onto the constraints by a multiplier mu (the GGL stabilization, as SolveTrapezoidalGGL); of order 4 in q and v, L-stable: it damps fast modes, also with steps of 70/omega of the mode; - 'Radau3': Radau IIA with the stages at 1/3 and the end of the step, the constraints as LobattoIIIA4; of order 3, L-stable. All of order 2 in the accelerations and multipliers (measured on a pendulum and a slider crank) and stiffly accurate: the end of the step is the last stage. With timeIntegration.automaticStepSize (the default) the step size is controlled by an estimate of the local error of the order of the method (#3250): the quadrature of the method, h sum_j b_j V_j, against the integral of the polynomial through the stage velocities of the previous and this step - for the Lobatto methods of degree 4, Simpson's error h^5/2880 v'''' -, and the same for the stage accelerations without constraints (with them, their stage values are of order 2, and the error of q decides); no extra solve. It is 0.3 to 0.6 times the true local error, for all step sizes; the global error is then of the size of the tolerances. The first step, without a previous one, by the embedded trapezoidal solution of the first (or the start) and the last stage, an error of order h^3. The PI controller and the settings as SolveTrapezoidalGGL; without it the steps of timeIntegration.numberOfSteps. Newton's method for the stage accelerations and multipliers (and mu) with the Jacobian of the system, the ODE2 rows scaled by h^2, by timeIntegration.newton as SolveTrapezoidalGGL; a step whose Newton iteration does not converge is repeated with a smaller step with automaticStepSize or adaptiveStep, else raises. Consistent initial accelerations and algebraic coordinates; the output as the solvers of exudyn.symbolics.solvers. The algebraic equations must depend on q and t only; ODE1 and data coordinates are not implemented
- **input**:
  - `system`: the system, a SymbolicSystemBase
  - `simulationSettings`: exudyn.SimulationSettings; None: the defaults
  - `method`: 'LobattoIIIA4', 'LobattoIIIC4-GGL' or 'Radau3'
- **output**: dict with 'time' (n_out), 'q', 'q_t', 'q_tt' (n_out x nODE2), with algebraic equations 'z', at the times of solution.file.writePeriod and the end, and the statistics 'steps', 'newtonIterations', 'jacobianEvaluations', 'rejectedSteps' (by Newton) and 'rejectedStepsError'


Relevant Examples (Ex) and TestModels (TM) with weblink to github: [`symbolicLobatto4Test.py`](https://github.com/jgerstmayr/EXUDYN/blob/master/python/TestModels/symbolicLobatto4Test.py) (TM)
